title: Dominic and the Ghost
premise: Kestrel Eriksen built her career laundering the untraceable—until her handler, Marcus Vane, dies and a calendar invite from his account summons her to a meeting she was never meant to survive. The network that trained her, called the Chantry, is purging its own, and Kestrel's name is on the list. To live, she must turn the network's clean money into a weapon, impersonating the dead handler's ghost inside their systems while a rival investigator closes in on her from outside. In the end she burns the Chantry's ledger and its masters, but only by surrendering her old identity entirely—emerging as someone new, with nothing clean left to hide behind.
about_author: Lena Eastwick is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade inside the quiet machinery of international finance before trading it for fiction. She writes thrillers about the people who keep dirty money clean, from a coastal town whose name she declines to share.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Seven years after walking away from the Chantry, Kestrel audits legitimate accounts by day and drinks by night. A meeting invitation arrives from her dead handler's email, scheduled for tomorrow at 9 a.m. The beat is dread disguised as curiosity—she knows the Chantry never sends reminders, only warnings.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Flashback-woven chapter: her recruitment at twenty-three, Vane teaching her that the best laundering looks like virtue. Present-day Kestrel tries to trace the invite and finds Vane's death certificate is real, but his digital life is still breathing. Beat: the past isn't past; it's just patient.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She goes to the meeting, telling herself it's surveillance, not surrender. The conference room holds a corpse—Vane's, preserved, staged—and a phone that rings when she sits. The voice gives her one task and a countdown. Beat: horror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Chantry's Rules
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She decodes the task: extract a ledger fragment from a Zurich shell before Friday. Interleaved, we learn the Chantry's structure—cells, handlers, a rule that failures die quietly. Beat: competence as comfort, and the first crack in it, because the task is designed to expose her.

chapters.title: Auditor
chapters.summary: Ilse Brandt's POV, introduced. Ilse is a Europol-adjacent investigator who has chased the Chantry's money for four years and just found Kestrel's signature inside a transaction that should be invisible. Beat: the hunter enters the story, and she's better than Kestrel hoped anyone would be.

chapters.title: Zurich, Briefly
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Zurich: she lifts the ledger fragment using Vane's ghost credentials and discovers the fragment names her—Kestrel Eriksen, asset, termination authorized. Beat: the mission was the trap; survival is now the only mission.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She decides to become Vane: resurrect his identity inside the Chantry's systems, speak with his voice, buy time. The chapter is a taut procedural of forgery and nerve. Beat: identity as armor—and the first taste of how much of herself she's about to lose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with a Chantry controller's POV interleave. Her Vane-impersonation works on the network's lower tier, but a controller named Sorrel tests her with a question only the real Vane could answer. Kestrel bluffs using a memory Vane once confessed drunk. Beat: triumph with a hairline fracture—someone is listening closely.

chapters.title: Ilse Closes
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse maps the Zurich breach to a person, not a ghost, and pulls Kestrel's sealed file. She finds the seven-year gap in Kestrel's history and starts pulling threads. Beat: two clocks now tick—Chantry countdown and Ilse's investigation—converging on the same woman.

chapters.title: Old Debt
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She seeks out Tomas, a fellow trainee who left the Chantry and survived, hiding as a marina mechanic. He refuses to help until she shows him the termination order; then he gives her a name—the Chantry's banker of record—and a warning: Sorrel trained them both. Beat: belonging, briefly, with someone who understands the cost.

chapters.title: The Banker of Record
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In Liechtenstein she confronts the banker, a meticulous old man who launders for the Chantry out of aesthetics, not greed. He confirms the purge is real and reveals the master ledger's location: a cold-storage vault keyed to biometric identity—Vane's. Beat: to open the vault, Kestrel must become Vane completely.

chapters.title: Becoming Vane
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A surgical, unsettling chapter: she acquires Vane's biometrics through a mortuary contact, and with each step the impersonation stops being a mask. Interleaved memories blur—was that her memory or his story? Beat: identity dissolving; the price of survival is paid in installments of self.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Parley
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Sorrel POV alternation. Sorrel, no longer fooled but intrigued, offers a deal: deliver Ilse to the Chantry and live. Kestrel stalls, learning Sorrel's motive—the purge is Sorrel consolidating power, not doctrine. Beat: temptation with teeth; betrayal offered as a lifeline.

chapters.title: The Other Investigator
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse confronts Kestrel in a train-station café, lays out everything, and offers the mirror deal: testify, and be protected. Kestrel sees the trap in both offers. Beat: the two women recognize each other—the only two people who see the whole machine.

chapters.title: Fragile Alliance
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Kestrel and Ilse strike a wary pact: Kestrel opens the vault, Ilse freezes the Chantry's exit capital so no one escapes with the money. They plan the vault entry for the night the Chantry's council convenes. Beat: trust built from mutual hostage-taking; belonging, invented rather than given.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Chantry finds Tomas first. Kestrel arrives to a burned boathouse and a message written in his hand before he died: the vault is a secondary site; the true ledger moves with the council. Grief hardens into fury. Beat: the cost of contact—everyone she reaches for burns.

chapters.title: Council of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, deep cover. Using Vane's credentials and Sorrel's grudging tolerance, Kestrel attends the council as the dead man's proxy. She watches the Chantry vote on its own future and learns the purge list includes Sorrel. Beat: the enemy is eating itself; opportunity dressed as chaos.

chapters.title: The Vault
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The vault sequence: Vane's biometrics open it, but the ledger is live-linked—opening it alerts the network. Kestrel copies the master ledger while alarms propagate, choosing exposure over incompleteness. Beat: point of no return, executed with cold precision.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Clean
chapters.summary: Ilse and Kestrel POV alternation. The ledger goes to Ilse; arrests cascade across four countries as the Chantry tries to move money that no longer moves. Sorrel, cornered, comes for Kestrel personally. Beat: climax rising—the machine dismantled, but its last hand still reaching.

chapters.title: Sorrel
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sorrel corners Kestrel in the marina where Tomas died. A duel of leverage and knives of information: Sorrel offers her old life back, fully restored. Kestrel refuses and ends it—Ilse's team arrives on her signal, not to save her but to witness. Beat: climax; survival chosen over restoration.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel testifies under a cooperation agreement, surrendering her history—real name, crimes, the whole seven years—into the record. The Chantry's remnants scatter; some money, she knows, will never be found. Beat: the price of survival paid in full; identity given away deliberately.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, epilogue. Months later, under a new name in a new coastal town, Kestrel receives a blank email from an account that doesn't exist—and deletes it without opening, then goes to work at an ordinary job, auditing ordinary money. Ilse sends a postcard: no text, just a lighthouse. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned; vigilance as a way of living free.
